name: geoboard
title: Geoboard
tagline: Peg board — square, isometric or circular pin-ring — with polygons formed by joining pegs; the band, fills and right-angle/parallel/equal-side marks all derived.
description: A geoboard / pin-board — a primary manipulative for constructing 2-D shapes and reading their properties. Pick a board: a square dot lattice (square-dots / square-lines), an isometric (triangular) dot lattice for isometric drawing (iso-dots / iso-lines), or a circular ring of pegs joined by chords (circular). For each shape you list the pegs the elastic band joins; the model derives the polygon outline, the shaded interior, and the property marks — right angles (corner squares), parallel sides (matching chevron arrows) and equal sides (matching ticks) — none of which can be authored, so a shape's marked properties always tell the truth. Multiple shapes overlap, each in its own colour; label a shape and occlude the label for a "name this shape" question, highlight one in amber, or show a derived property summary. v1 is static (with host-driven staged builds): no drag, no answer-on-the-board mode yet.
whenToUse: Reach for this to construct polygons on a grid and to teach the properties of 2-D shapes — sides, corners (vertices), right angles, parallel sides and equal sides — the way a geoboard / pin-board / dotty-paper lesson does. Choose the board with board.type: "square-dots" (plain square pin lattice), "square-lines" (the same with a faint square grid), "iso-dots" / "iso-lines" (an isometric / triangular lattice — for equilateral triangles, rhombi, hexagons, parallelograms and isometric drawing of 2-D polygons), or "circular" (a ring of board.pins pegs, e.g. 8 or 12, joined by chords). Set board.cols / board.rows (pegs across / up) for grid boards, board.pins for a circular board. Then write shapes: each shape's points are the pegs the band visits, in order — [x, y] on a grid (x right, y up, [0,0] bottom-left) or [pin] (0…pins−1, from the top, clockwise) on a circular board. Everything else is derived: turn on marks.rightAngles / marks.parallel / marks.equalSides to draw the property marks (matching chevrons for parallel families, matching ticks for equal-length families, corner squares for right angles), set fill to shade the interior, properties for a derived sides/angles summary line. Common configurations: properties — a labelled quadrilateral with marks.rightAngles + marks.parallel + properties (square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezium, kite); construct — an empty board (no shapes) with a caption ("make a triangle with one right angle") as an answer space; name it — label the shape and set occludeLabel, showing the marks so pupils name it from its properties; isometric — an iso board with a triangle / parallelogram / hexagon; circular — an inscribed square or triangle on a 12-pin ring; overlap / compare — two or three shapes, each its own colour. Keep the same board (type and size) across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one board. A staged build reads well: open on the empty board, then add one peg / side per stage until the shape is closed, then shade it and add the marks (give later stages a larger points list, then fill / marks). Switch model when the teaching changes: for coordinates and reading/plotting points use graphing/coordinate-grid; for area by counting squares use a squared-grid area model; for a solid drawn from unit cubes use geometry/isometric-cubes; for reflection symmetry use geometry/symmetry. Synonyms a teacher might use: geoboard, geo-board, pin board, pinboard, nail board, dotty paper, dot paper, square dots, isometric paper, triangular dots, elastic band, rubber band, make a shape, construct a polygon, properties of shapes, sides and corners, right angle, parallel sides, equal sides, quadrilaterals, triangles, circular geoboard, pin-circle, chords.

board.description: The peg board. Defaults to a 5×5 square dot lattice if omitted.

type.description: "square-dots": a square lattice of pegs. "square-lines": the same with a faint square grid drawn through the pegs. "iso-dots": an isometric (triangular) lattice of pegs — vertical columns, the standard isometric dot paper for drawing 2-D polygons. "iso-lines": the same with the faint triangular grid drawn. "circular": a ring of pegs (no lattice), joined by chords. Default "square-dots".

cols.description: Number of pegs ACROSS the board (the x range is 0…cols−1). Grid boards only. Default 5.

rows.description: Number of pegs UP the board (the y range is 0…rows−1). Grid boards only. Default 5.

pins.description: Number of pegs evenly spaced around the RING — circular board only (e.g. 8 or 12). Pin 0 is at the top (12 o'clock); pins are numbered clockwise. Default 12.

items.description: One peg the band hooks on. On a GRID board (square-*/iso-*) write [x, y] — column then row, x to the right, y UPWARD, origin [0, 0] at the bottom-left peg. On a CIRCULAR board write [pin] — a single index 0…pins−1 starting at the top (12 o'clock) and going clockwise.

points.description: The pegs the elastic band visits, in order. Two pegs draw a single segment; three or more draw a polygon (closed back to the first by default). Each entry is a peg reference — [x, y] on a grid board, [pin] on a circular board.

closed.description: Join the last peg back to the first (a closed polygon). Default true for 3+ pegs. Set false for an OPEN path / polyline — the band hooked across pegs without closing (e.g. demonstrating the open-polygon misconception, or a path being built up). Ignored for a 2-peg segment.

fill.description: Shade the polygon's interior (bold border + light tinted fill, in the shape's own colour). Default false (outline only). Only meaningful for a closed polygon of 3+ pegs.

label.description: A name drawn at the polygon's centroid — e.g. "A", "R", or a shape name like "trapezium". The TEXT is authored (a shape's name cannot be derived); its POSITION is computed. Omit for an unlabelled shape.

occludeLabel.description: Render the label as "?" — the "name this shape" / "which shape is it?" hook. The shape and its marks stay visible. Default false. Only meaningful with label.

highlight.description: Draw this shape's band (and fill, if any) in amber — emphasis / "this is the answer". Reserved colour; use sparingly. Default false.

marks.description: Which DERIVED property marks to draw on this shape. Each is computed from the geometry, never authored — so they always tell the truth about the shape.

rightAngles.description: Mark every interior right angle with a small square corner symbol (detected where two sides meet at 90°). Default false.

parallel.description: Mark parallel sides with matching chevron arrows — one arrow on the first parallel family, two on the second, and so on (detected from the side directions; only families of 2+ parallel sides are marked). Default false.

equalSides.description: Mark equal-length sides with matching tick hatches — one tick on the first equal-length family, two on the second, and so on (detected from the side lengths; only families of 2+ equal sides are marked). Default false.

properties.description: Show a DERIVED one-line property summary for this shape beneath the figure — its number of sides, right angles, pairs of parallel sides and equal sides (the verbal twin of the marks). Default false.

shapes.description: The shapes on the board, each an elastic band joining pegs. Omit (or pass an empty array) for an EMPTY board — an answer space for pupils to make a shape themselves. Multiple shapes are drawn in distinct colours (the first blue, then teal, purple, coral) so overlapping shapes read apart; use highlight to amber the one that matters.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the board; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure (wraps), e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
